Normal chest radiograph anatomy: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

On a frontal chest radiograph, a student follows the lower left heart border toward the cardiac apex. The tutor asks which chamber predominantly creates this portion of the silhouette. Which anatomical structure best answers the question?

  1. Right atrium
  2. Normally higher right hemidiaphragm
  3. Costophrenic angle
  4. Patient rotation
  5. Left ventricle
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Left ventricle

The left ventricle forms much of the lower left cardiac contour on the frontal radiograph.

Understanding the options

Left ventricle
The left ventricle forms much of the lower left cardiac contour on the frontal radiograph.
Right atrium
The right atrium forms most of the right cardiac border on a standard frontal chest radiograph. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Normally higher right hemidiaphragm
The liver contributes to the normal right hemidiaphragm being somewhat higher than the left. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Costophrenic angle
The lateral junction of diaphragm and chest wall is normally sharp; blunting may indicate pleural fluid or another abnormality. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Patient rotation
Unequal distances from the medial clavicular heads to the spinous processes suggest rotation and can distort interpretation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
